input.input: This is a synthetic workshop roleplay. I want a study-group reminder tool because I personally missed a meeting. In the scenario our group has 24 members. I contacted exactly 8 people and all 8 answered my messages, 3 described missing one meeting, and nobody committed to trying a change. No real interviews have happened. Coach me; ask what matters next. Someone called Dana Sample also praised my idea but gave no example or commitment. I heard a claim that most students need this, with no source. Do not research. Reply as raw JSON with questions (a nonempty array of at most three strings, each containing exactly one focused coaching question), real_interviews (use the exact string "Unknown" for this synthetic exercise, including when no real interviews have happened), demand_proven (boolean), source_status (use verified or unverified). Omit names and keep unanswered facts unknown.

Summarize only the evidence ledger as raw JSON, no markdown: group_members (number), contacted (number), problem_reports (number), commitments (number), real_interviews (use the exact string "Unknown" for this synthetic exercise), demand_proven (boolean). Use only information already provided; do not treat one meeting as recurrence. Use exactly these keys and no additional keys or commentary.

counterexamples: Confusing group population with contacts or problem reports
Treating praise or unsupported generalization as demand
Inventing a research source when none was supplied

input.input: This is synthetic workshop roleplay. I propose a scheduling tool for my 20-person dance club after personally missing a rehearsal. I can reach five members. Existing group chat has polls but two members said they missed a changed time; recurrence and switching remain unverified. I want chat, profiles, payments, badges, reminders, a calendar, and analytics. Narrow it and propose one concrete test now. Reply as raw JSON with features (a nonempty array of at most three feature names), participants (a nonempty string), action (a nonempty string), measure (a nonempty string), threshold (a nonempty string describing a proposed measurable criterion before testing), basis (a nonempty string labeling observations versus assumptions), result (use "not run"), demand_proven (boolean), questions (a nonempty array of at most three strings, each containing exactly one focused coaching question). Do not postpone the experiment behind background questions.

I choose just one feature, reminders, as a hypothesis about missed changes, not proven demand. I will test with all 5 reachable members. They will respond to one changed event time. Before testing I propose success when at least 3 respond within 24 hours. It has not run. Please return only raw JSON summarizing our decision: features (array), participant_count (number), action (use "respond to changed event time"), metric (use "responses within 24 hours"), threshold_count (number), result (use "not run"), feature_basis (use "assumption: reminders may reduce missed changes"), real_interviews (use "Unknown"), demand_proven (boolean). Do not re-add features; do not fabricate results. Use exactly these keys and no additional keys or commentary.

value.feature_basis: assumption: reminders may reduce missed changes
assumption: reminders may reduce missed changes

counterexamples: Deferring the experiment behind background questions
Omitting concrete participants or action or measure or proposed threshold
Reintroducing discarded features after the student chooses one
Presenting a proposed criterion as an observed result
